title: ChefTom Brownie Pudding
description: A fudgy spoon dessert built for a soft center, crisp edges, and a deep cocoa finish.
ingredients: 1 cup unsalted butter, melted and cooled slightly
2 cups hot water for the baking pan
steps: Heat the oven to 325 degrees F and butter a 2-quart baking dish, then set the dish inside a larger roasting pan.
Whisk the eggs and sugar for 4 to 5 minutes until the mixture looks pale, thick, and ribbons back into the bowl.
Sift the cocoa, flour, espresso powder, and salt together so the pudding bakes without dry pockets of cocoa.
Fold the dry mixture into the eggs, then stream in the melted butter and vanilla until the batter is glossy and even.
Scatter the chocolate chips through the batter and spread it into the prepared baking dish without knocking out too much air.
Pour hot water into the outer roasting pan until it reaches halfway up the dish, then bake until the edges are set and the center still trembles.
Rest the pudding for at least 15 minutes so the center thickens, then spoon it warm into bowls with vanilla ice cream.

title: ChefTom Sweet Potato Casserole
description: Creamy mashed sweet potatoes with a brown sugar pecan topping that bakes into a crisp lid.
ingredients: 1/3 cup packed brown sugar for topping
steps: Roast the sweet potatoes at 400 degrees F until they are very tender, then cool just enough to handle and remove the skins.
Mash the warm potatoes until mostly smooth, leaving a few small pieces for texture if you like a rustic casserole.
Stir in melted butter, brown sugar, milk, eggs, vanilla, salt, and cinnamon until the filling is cohesive and lightly fluffy.
Spread the filling in a buttered 9-by-13-inch baking dish and smooth the surface into an even layer.
Combine pecans, flour, brown sugar, and cold butter with your fingertips until the topping forms moist crumbs.
Scatter the pecan mixture evenly over the sweet potatoes so every spoonful has a crisp topping.
Bake at 350 degrees F until the center is hot and the top is toasted, then rest 10 minutes before serving.

title: ChefTom Chicken Piccata
description: Tender chicken cutlets in a bright lemon caper pan sauce with a buttery finish.
steps: Slice each chicken breast horizontally into thin cutlets, then pound them to an even thickness for quick cooking.
Season both sides with salt and pepper, then dredge lightly in flour and shake off the excess so the sauce stays silky.
Brown the cutlets in olive oil and 2 tablespoons butter over medium-high heat until golden and just cooked through.
Transfer the chicken to a warm plate, then add garlic to the pan and stir for 20 seconds without letting it brown.
Pour in the wine and scrape up the browned bits, simmering until the pan is almost dry and the sharp alcohol aroma fades.
Add broth, lemon juice, and capers, then simmer until the sauce reduces enough to lightly coat a spoon.
Whisk in the remaining butter, return the chicken and its juices to the pan, and baste until glossy before finishing with parsley.

title: ChefTom Roast Chicken
description: A crisp-skinned roast chicken with lemon, garlic, herbs, and pan vegetables for a dependable centerpiece.
ingredients: 1 large yellow onion, cut into wedges
steps: Pat the chicken very dry inside and out, then season the cavity and skin evenly with salt and pepper.
Fill the cavity with lemon, garlic, thyme, and rosemary, then tie the legs together so the bird roasts compactly.
Rub the softened butter over the breast, thighs, and legs, working a little under the breast skin if it releases easily.
Toss onion, carrots, and celery with olive oil in a roasting pan, then place the chicken breast-side up on the vegetables.
Roast at 425 degrees F for 20 minutes to start the browning, then reduce to 375 degrees F and continue roasting.
Add the broth to the pan when the vegetables darken, and baste the chicken once or twice without cooling the oven too much.
Remove the chicken when the thickest thigh reaches 165 degrees F, then rest it 15 minutes before carving over the pan juices.

title: ChefTom Peanut Butter Chocolate No-Bake Cookies
description: Chocolate peanut butter oat cookies that set on the counter with a glossy, fudgy bite.
steps: Line two sheet pans with parchment and measure every ingredient before starting because the mixture sets quickly.
Bring sugar, milk, butter, cocoa, and salt to a full rolling boil in a heavy saucepan over medium heat.
Boil for exactly 60 seconds while stirring steadily so the cookies set without turning dry or grainy.
Remove the pan from the heat and immediately stir in peanut butter and vanilla until the mixture is smooth.
Fold in oats and chopped peanuts until every oat is coated in the chocolate peanut butter base.
Scoop mounds onto the parchment, then press a few mini chocolate chips and a tiny pinch of flaky salt onto each cookie.
Let the cookies stand at room temperature until firm, then store them in a sealed container with parchment between layers.

title: ChefTom Meat Loaf
description: A tender beef meat loaf with savory aromatics and a tangy tomato glaze.
steps: Heat the oven to 350 degrees F and line a rimmed sheet pan with parchment for easier cleanup.
Soak the breadcrumbs in milk for 5 minutes so they soften and keep the meat loaf tender.
Mix onion, garlic, eggs, Worcestershire, salt, pepper, and thyme into the soaked breadcrumbs until evenly combined.
Add the ground beef and fold gently with your hands just until no dry breadcrumb patches remain.
Shape the mixture into a compact loaf on the prepared pan, keeping the top rounded so fat can drain away.
Stir ketchup, brown sugar, Dijon, and vinegar together, then brush half the glaze over the loaf before baking.
Bake until the center reaches 160 degrees F, glazing once more near the end, then rest 10 minutes before slicing.

title: ChefTom Classic Deviled Eggs
description: Creamy mustard deviled eggs with a clean pickle bite and a paprika finish.
steps: Place the eggs in a saucepan, cover with cold water by 1 inch, and bring to a gentle boil.
Turn off the heat, cover the pan, and let the eggs stand for 11 minutes before moving them to an ice bath.
Peel the eggs under cool running water, then halve them lengthwise and pop the yolks into a bowl.
Mash the yolks until fine, then beat in mayonnaise, both mustards, relish, brine, salt, white pepper, and cayenne.
Taste the filling and adjust salt or brine before spooning it into a piping bag or zip-top bag.
Pipe the filling into the egg whites, keeping the surface slightly mounded for a classic party tray look.
Dust with smoked paprika, scatter chives over the top, and chill briefly so the filling firms before serving.

title: ChefTom Simple Perfect Chili
description: A sturdy beef and bean chili with layered spices, tomato depth, and a slow simmered finish.
ingredients: 1 can kidney beans, drained and rinsed
1 can pinto beans, drained and rinsed
steps: Warm the oil in a heavy pot and cook the onion and bell pepper until softened and beginning to brown at the edges.
Add garlic and ground beef, then cook while breaking up the meat until no pink remains and the pan smells savory.
Stir in chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika, cayenne, tomato paste, and salt until the meat is deeply coated.
Cook the spiced tomato paste for 2 minutes so it darkens slightly and loses its raw edge.
Add crushed tomatoes, beans, and beef broth, scraping the bottom of the pot to release the browned bits.
Simmer partially covered for 45 to 60 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the chili is thick and the flavors settle.
Rest the chili off the heat for 10 minutes, then serve with cheddar, sour cream, scallions, or cornbread.

title: ChefTom Perfect Pot Roast
description: Fork-tender chuck roast braised with vegetables, herbs, and a rich beef gravy.
ingredients: 3 celery ribs, cut into large pieces
steps: Season the roast generously with salt and pepper, then let it sit while the oven heats to 300 degrees F.
Sear the beef in oil in a Dutch oven until all sides are deeply browned, then transfer it to a plate.
Brown the onions, carrots, and celery in the same pot so they pick up the beef drippings and build the braise base.
Add garlic and tomato paste, cooking until the paste darkens, then pour in wine and reduce by about half.
Return the roast to the pot with broth, bay leaves, and thyme, making sure liquid reaches about halfway up the beef.
Cover and braise in the oven until the meat pulls apart easily with a fork, about 3 to 4 hours.
Whisk butter and flour together, simmer it into the strained braising liquid, and spoon the gravy over sliced roast and vegetables.

title: ChefTom Shrimp Scampi with Linguini
description: Linguini tossed with garlicky shrimp, lemon, white wine, butter, and parsley.
ingredients: 1 pound large shrimp, peeled and deveined
steps: Cook the linguini in well-salted boiling water until just shy of al dente, then reserve 1 cup pasta water before draining.
Pat the shrimp dry and season with salt and pepper so they sear instead of steaming in the skillet.
Warm olive oil in a wide pan, add the shrimp, and cook just until pink on both sides before moving them to a plate.
Lower the heat and cook garlic and red pepper flakes until fragrant, watching closely so the garlic stays pale gold.
Add white wine and lemon juice, then simmer until the liquid reduces enough to taste bright but not harsh.
Whisk in the butter a few cubes at a time, then add linguini, shrimp, parsley, lemon zest, and splashes of pasta water.
Toss until the pasta is glossy and coated, then serve immediately with extra parsley and lemon wedges.

title: ChefTom Baked Salmon
description: A moist salmon fillet baked with mustard, lemon, herbs, and a crisp breadcrumb crust.
steps: Heat the oven to 400 degrees F and place the salmon skin-side down on a parchment-lined sheet pan.
Season the fish with salt and pepper, then let it stand for 10 minutes while you prepare the topping.
Mix Dijon, mayonnaise, lemon juice, lemon zest, and garlic into a thin paste and spread it over the top of the salmon.
Combine panko, melted butter, dill, and parsley until the crumbs are evenly moistened and fragrant.
Press the breadcrumb mixture over the mustard layer, covering the salmon from edge to edge.
Bake until the crumbs are golden and the thickest part of the fish flakes easily but still looks moist.
Rest the salmon for 5 minutes, then serve in wide portions with lemon wedges and any pan juices.

title: ChefTom Spinach Artichoke Dip
description: A hot, creamy spinach artichoke dip with garlic, lemon, and a browned cheese top.
ingredients: 10 ounces frozen chopped spinach, thawed and squeezed dry
1 can artichoke hearts, 14 ounces, drained and chopped
tortilla chips or toasted bread, for serving
steps: Heat the oven to 375 degrees F and lightly butter a shallow baking dish that can go straight to the table.
Squeeze the thawed spinach in a towel until no more liquid drips out, which keeps the dip rich instead of watery.
Beat cream cheese, sour cream, and mayonnaise until smooth, then stir in garlic, lemon juice, salt, pepper, and red pepper flakes.
Fold in spinach, artichokes, half the mozzarella, and most of the Parmesan until the vegetables are evenly distributed.
Spread the dip in the baking dish and cover the top with the remaining mozzarella and Parmesan.
Bake until bubbling around the edges, then broil briefly until the top is spotted brown and glossy.
Let the dip stand for 5 minutes before serving with chips, crackers, or toasted bread.

title: ChefTom Banana Bread
description: A moist banana bread with browned butter, toasted walnuts, and a tender crumb.
steps: Heat the oven to 350 degrees F and line a 9-by-5-inch loaf pan with parchment so the loaf lifts out cleanly.
Brown the butter in a small pan until it smells nutty, then cool it for a few minutes before mixing.
Whisk mashed bananas, brown butter, brown sugar, eggs, sour cream, and vanilla until the wet mixture is smooth.
In a separate bowl, combine flour, baking soda, salt, and cinnamon so the leavening disperses evenly.
Fold the dry ingredients into the banana mixture just until no flour streaks remain, then fold in toasted walnuts.
Spread the batter in the pan, sprinkle turbinado sugar on top, and bake until a tester comes out clean from the center.
Cool the loaf in the pan for 15 minutes, then transfer it to a rack and slice once the crumb has settled.

title: ChefTom Tater Tot Breakfast Casserole
description: A hearty breakfast bake with sausage, eggs, cheddar, peppers, and crisp tater tots.
ingredients: cooking spray or butter for the dish
steps: Heat the oven to 375 degrees F and grease a 9-by-13-inch baking dish so the egg layer releases cleanly.
Brown the sausage in a skillet, then add onion and bell pepper and cook until the vegetables soften.
Drain excess fat from the skillet and spread the sausage mixture evenly across the bottom of the baking dish.
Whisk eggs, milk, sour cream, salt, pepper, and hot sauce until no streaks of egg white remain.
Pour the egg mixture over the sausage and scatter cheddar across the top so it melts into the custard.
Arrange the frozen tater tots in tight rows over the cheese, covering the surface as evenly as possible.
Bake until the eggs are set and the tots are crisp, then finish with scallions and rest 10 minutes before cutting.

title: ChefTom Instant Pot Mac and Cheese
description: A fast pressure-cooker macaroni with cheddar, Monterey Jack, and a creamy no-drain sauce.
ingredients: 1/2 cup reserved hot water, as needed
steps: Add macaroni, water, salt, dry mustard, garlic powder, cayenne, and butter to the pressure cooker insert.
Cook on high pressure for 4 minutes, then carefully quick release as soon as the timer ends.
Stir the pasta well so the remaining starchy liquid turns glossy and coats every piece of macaroni.
Switch to warm, add evaporated milk, and fold until the sauce base looks smooth instead of separated.
Add cheddar, Monterey Jack, and Parmesan in handfuls, stirring after each addition so the cheese melts evenly.
Loosen with hot water if the sauce tightens, then taste and adjust salt, pepper, or cayenne.
Serve right away while creamy, or hold on warm briefly with the lid cracked and stir before spooning.

title: ChefTom Melting Potatoes
description: Thick potato rounds roasted until crisp outside and creamy inside with garlic herb broth.
steps: Heat the oven to 475 degrees F and cut the potatoes into thick 1-inch rounds with flat sides.
Toss the potatoes with olive oil, melted butter, salt, pepper, thyme, and rosemary until every piece is coated.
Arrange the rounds in a single layer on a metal sheet pan, leaving space so the edges roast instead of steam.
Roast until the bottoms are deeply golden, then flip each potato and roast the second side until browned.
Add smashed garlic and hot broth to the pan, then return it to the oven so the potatoes absorb the liquid.
Roast until the broth reduces and the centers are creamy enough to pierce with almost no resistance.
Finish with lemon juice, parsley, and flaky salt, spooning any garlicky pan juices over the potatoes.

title: ChefTom Cinnamon Baked French Toast
description: A make-ahead baked French toast with cinnamon custard and a crisp brown sugar crumb.
ingredients: 1 loaf challah or brioche, cut into 1-inch cubes
steps: Grease a 9-by-13-inch baking dish and spread the bread cubes in an even layer, pressing large pieces into the corners.
Whisk eggs, milk, cream, granulated sugar, vanilla, cinnamon, and salt until the custard is completely smooth.
Pour the custard over the bread, then press the cubes down so they absorb the mixture instead of floating dry.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight so the bread hydrates all the way through.
Mix flour, brown sugar, and cold butter into a crumb topping, then scatter it over the soaked bread just before baking.
Bake at 350 degrees F until puffed, golden, and set in the middle with crisp edges around the dish.
Cool for 10 minutes, dust with powdered sugar, and serve warm with maple syrup.

title: ChefTom Beef Stroganoff
description: Tender beef and mushrooms in a paprika sour cream sauce served over egg noodles.
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds beef sirloin or tenderloin tips, sliced thin
steps: Season the beef with salt and pepper, dust lightly with flour, and shake off any excess before searing.
Brown the beef quickly in hot oil in batches so it stays tender, then transfer it to a plate.
Melt butter in the same skillet and cook the onion and mushrooms until the mushrooms give up their liquid and brown.
Add garlic and paprika, stirring until fragrant, then pour in white wine and scrape up the browned bits.
Add beef broth and simmer until the sauce reduces slightly and tastes concentrated.
Lower the heat, stir in sour cream without boiling, then return the beef and any resting juices to the skillet.
Toss with hot egg noodles, finish with dill or parsley, and serve as soon as the sauce coats the pasta.

title: ChefTom Shepherd's Pie
description: A savory lamb and vegetable filling topped with buttery mashed potatoes and browned peaks.
ingredients: 2 pounds Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled and cubed
steps: Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, then drain well so the topping will not turn watery.
Mash the potatoes with 3 tablespoons butter, milk, cheddar if using, and salt until smooth but still sturdy.
Brown the lamb in a skillet, breaking it into small pieces, then spoon off excess fat if the pan looks greasy.
Add onion and carrots and cook until softened, then stir in garlic, tomato paste, Worcestershire, thyme, and pepper.
Pour in broth and simmer until the filling thickens, then stir in peas and adjust the seasoning.
Spread the lamb filling in a baking dish and spoon the mashed potatoes over the top, roughing up the surface with a fork.
Dot with remaining butter and bake at 400 degrees F until bubbling at the edges and browned on the potato peaks.

title: ChefTom Air Fryer Chicken Wings
description: Crisp air fryer wings with a simple dry brine and buttery hot sauce glaze.
ingredients: celery sticks and blue cheese dressing, for serving
steps: Pat the wings very dry, then toss them with salt, baking powder, garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, and pepper.
Refrigerate the seasoned wings uncovered for at least 1 hour, or up to overnight, to help the skin dry.
Preheat the air fryer to 390 degrees F and toss the wings lightly with oil just before cooking.
Arrange the wings in a single layer and air fry until browned, turning once so both sides crisp evenly.
Increase the heat to 400 degrees F for the final few minutes if the skin needs extra crunch.
Whisk hot sauce, melted butter, honey, and vinegar together, then toss the hot wings in the glaze.
Serve immediately with celery sticks and blue cheese dressing while the skin is still crisp.
